newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Chester plans JSE listing via Solchem shell.
newsitem.headline: Chester plans JSE listing via Solchem shell.

text.p: Investment company Chester Industries Ltd said on Thursday it would list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in September via the listed cash shell Solchem Ltd.

Chester chairman Milton Levine and director Carlos dos Santos would acquire some 33.28 million shares or 79.8 percent of Solchem from printing and publishing firm CTP Holdings for 130 cents a share, effective September 1.
These shares would be renounced immediately in favour of other investors at the same price.
Chester, which would list on the JSE's investment trust sector, would have 85 million rand available in cash resources after the listing.
The company said in a statement that its policy was to acquire minority shareholdings in under capitalised owner-managed and controlled medium-sized companies for between 1.5 and 15 million rand.
The listing was aimed at raising cash to fund further investment opportunities, it said.
The company has an investment in listed firm Softline and plans another listing in the near future using the Bloch Ltd cash shell which Chester and others have acquired.
A pre-listing statement will be published in due course.
